passages.note: Bill details page names Glick as author of the enacted abortion bill and lists the effective date of Public Law 179(ss).

passages.provision_quote: (A) based on reasonable medical judgment, performing the abortion is necessary to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life;
passages.note: Enrolled act text: abortion is a criminal act except for risk-to-life/health, lethal fetal anomaly, or (within 10 weeks) rape or incest; deleted text excluded from the provision quote.
Senate roll call 58 shows Glick voting Yea on concurrence, final passage 28-19.

rows.reasoning: Glick authored SB 1(ss) (2022 First Special Session) and voted Yea on its final concurrence passage (28-19); the enacted law makes abortion a criminal act except where necessary 'to prevent any serious health risk to the pregnant woman or to save the pregnant woman's life,' or, within ten weeks, where the pregnancy results from rape or incest. This matches the rung banning abortion except in cases of rape, incest, or a serious risk to the mother's life, and excludes the rungs keeping abortion broadly legal and the rung allowing no exceptions at all.
